q: 361. The drop of a flat slab may have thickness........ more than the rest of the slab
explain: The drop panel is a thickened portion of the slab around the column designed to resist negative moments and punching shear; it typically increases slab thickness by 25% to 50%.

q: 362. According to I.S.: 456-2000, in the case of slender columns, the permissible stresses in steel and concrete are reduced by multiplying with a coefficient Cr given by
explain: The reduction factor Cr accounts for the buckling tendency of slender columns. The standard formula relates the effective length (le) to the least radius of gyration (rmin).

q: 363. When the pile is suspended from two points, the minimum B.M. will occur if the overhang from each support is
explain: For a beam or pile suspended at two points, the maximum positive and negative bending moments are minimized when the overhang is approximately 0.207L (often rounded to 0.206L).

q: 364. The precast concrete piles are generally used for a maximum design load of about...... except for large prestressed piles
explain: Standard precast RC piles are typically designed for loads up to 80 tonnes. For higher loads, prestressed piles or cast-in-situ piles are preferred.

q: 365. On designing reinforced concrete piles as a column, it is considered as
options: fixed at one end and hinged at the other end
explain: A pile is usually considered fixed at the bottom (embedded in hard strata) and hinged at the top (connection with the pile cap) for effective length calculations.

q: 366. The length of a reinforced concrete pile is taken as ............ the length embedded in firm stratum.
explain: In certain design simplified assumptions, the effective length of the pile is taken as half of the total length if the soil provides significant lateral restraint.

q: 367. For reinforced piles having length up to 30 times its width, the main longitudinal reinforcement should not be less than ............ of the gross cross-sectional area of the pile.
explain: Code provisions for RC piles generally require a minimum longitudinal steel percentage of 1.25% to ensure structural integrity during driving and service.

q: 368. The ultimate moment resisting capacity of a simple supported pre-stressed concreted beam is obtained by using
options: stress-strain relationship of concrete and steel
explain: The analysis of prestressed sections at the ultimate limit state requires satisfying both equilibrium of forces and the compatibility of strains between steel and concrete.

q: 369. The cube strength of the concrete used for pre-stressed member should not be less than
explain: As per IS codes, the minimum grade for post-tensioned work is M30-M35, but in many contexts, 25-30 MPa is cited as the lowest threshold for basic prestressed applications.

q: 370. In post-tensioned pre-stressed concrete beam, the end block zone is the zone between the end of the beam and the section where
options: shape of the cross-section of beam
explain: The end block is the region where concentrated anchorage forces disperse into uniform longitudinal stress across the full section (Saint Venant's Principle).

q: 371. The propagation of a shear crack in a pre-stressed concrete member depends upon
options: shape of the cross-section of beam
explain: The shape of the cross-section (like I-beams) significantly influences the distribution of principal stresses and how shear cracks initiate and propagate.

q: 372. The major loss of pre-stress is caused due to
explain: Loss of prestress occurs due to immediate factors (elastic shortening) and time-dependent factors (creep, shrinkage, and steel relaxation).

q: 373. Columns may be made of plain concrete of their unsupported length do not exceed their least lateral dimension
explain: According to IS 456, a compression member is called a 'pedestal' if its unsupported length is less than 3 times its least lateral dimension; these can be plain concrete.

q: 374. According to load factor method, the permissible load W on a short column reinforced with longitudinal bars and lateral stirrups, is
options: stress in concrete x area of concrete
stress in steel x area of steel
stress in concrete x area of concrete + stress in steel x area of steel
explain: The load factor (Ultimate Strength) method calculates capacity by summing the ultimate strengths contributed by both the concrete and the longitudinal steel.

q: 375. A column is regarded as long column if the ratio of its effective length and lateral dimension, exceeds
explain: A column is classified as 'long' (or slender) if the ratio of effective length to the least lateral dimension exceeds 12 (rounded to 15 in some older or specific texts).

q: 376. If the size of column is reduced above the floor, the main bars of the columns, are
options: bent inward at the floor level
stopped just below the floor level and separate lap bars provided
explain: Depending on the degree of offset, bars can be cranked (bent) or terminated with new starter bars provided to maintain continuity.

q: 377. The pitch of the main bars in a simply supported slab, should not exceed its effective depth by
explain: IS 456 specifies that the maximum spacing (pitch) for main tension reinforcement in slabs must not exceed 3 times the effective depth (3d) or 300 mm.

q: 378. Distribution reinforcement in a simply supported slab, is provided to distribute
explain: Secondary reinforcement (distribution bars) helps spread concentrated loads and controls cracking caused by temperature changes and concrete shrinkage.

q: 379. The modular ratio m of a concrete whose permissible compressive stress is C, may be obtained from the equation
explain: The standard IS 456 formula for the modular ratio in Working Stress Method is m = 280 / (3 * sigma_cbc), where C is the permissible stress.

q: 380. For M 150 grade concrete (1 : 2 : 4) the moment of resistance factor is
explain: The Q factor (Moment of Resistance factor) for M15 grade concrete in WSM (balanced section) is approximately 8.5.

q: 381. If the maximum bending moment of a simply supported slab is M kg. cm, the effective depth of the slab is
explain: From the formula M = Qbd², for unit width (b=100cm), d = √(M / 100Q).

q: 382. The floor slab of a building is supported on reinforced cement floor beams. The ratio of the end and intermediate spans is kept
explain: To achieve a more uniform bending moment across continuous spans, the end span is typically made slightly shorter (around 0.9 of intermediate span).

q: 383. The maximum ratio of span to depth of a cantilever slab, is
explain: For deflection control, the span-to-effective depth ratio for a cantilever is restricted to 7 (for basic values) or up to 12 depending on loading/reinforcement.

q: 384. The amount of reinforcement for main bars in a slab, is based upon
explain: Design reinforcement is always calculated to resist the maximum bending moment occurring at any critical section of the slab.

q: 385. The percentage minimum reinforcement of the gross sectional area in slabs, is
explain: IS 456 specifies 0.15% for mild steel bars and 0.12% for HYSD bars. 0.15% is the standard general minimum.

q: 386. In a slab, the pitch of the main reinforcement should not exceed its effective depth
explain: To ensure proper load distribution and crack control, the spacing of main bars is limited to 3 times the effective depth.

q: 387. The transverse reinforcement provided at right angles to the main reinforcement
explain: Transverse reinforcement (distribution steel) performs all these functions: load spreading, temperature resistance, and shrinkage control.

q: 388. If the diameter of the main reinforcement in a slab is 16 mm, the concrete cover to main bars is
explain: Nominal cover should generally not be less than the diameter of the bar (16 mm in this case) or the specified environmental cover (usually 15-20mm for slabs).

q: 389. The weight of reinforced concrete, is generally taken as
explain: Plain concrete is 2400 kg/m³, while reinforced concrete (RCC) is taken as 2500 kg/m³ to account for the higher density of steel.

q: 390. If the ratio of long and short spans of a two way slab with corners held down is r, the actual reduction of B.M. is given by
explain: Based on Marcus's method for two-way slabs, the reduction factor involves the span ratio raised to the fourth power.

q: 391. According to I.S. 456, slabs which span in two directions with corners held down, are assumed to be divided in each direction into middle strips and edge strips such that the width of the middle strip, is
options: half of the width of the slab
two-third of the width of the slab
three-fourth of the width of the slab
four-fifth of the width of the slab
explain: IS 456 defines the middle strip as the central 3/4th (75%) of the span in each direction.

q: 392. If the sides of a slab simply supported on edges and spanning in two directions are equal, the maximum bending moment is multiplied by
explain: For a square slab (r=1), the load is shared equally in both directions, effectively halving the moment compared to a one-way slab.

q: 393. Design of a two way slab simply supported on edge and having no provision to prevent the corners from lifting is made by
explain: The Rankine-Grashoff theory is used for slabs where corners are free to lift, which assumes no torsional resistance at corners.

q: 394. The effective width of a column strip of flat slab, is
options: one-fourth the width of the panel
half the width of the panel
explain: In flat slab design, the column strip is defined as having a width equal to 50% (half) of the panel width.

q: 395. A circular slab subjected to external loading deflects to form a
explain: Due to uniform loading and radial symmetry, the elastic deflection curve of a circular plate/slab follows a paraboloid of revolution.

q: 396. If the ratio of the span to the overall depth does not exceed 10, the stiffness of the beam will ordinarily be satisfactory in case of a
explain: Cantilever beams are most critical for deflection; keeping L/D ≤ 10 (or specifically 7 for basic limits) usually ensures adequate stiffness.

q: 397. The ratio of the breadth to effective depth of a beam is kept
explain: For economical and structural efficiency, the breadth of a beam is typically half (0.50) of its effective depth.

q: 398. For initial estimate for a beam design, the width is assumed
explain: A common rule of thumb for initial sizing of beam width is approximately 1/30th of the span.

q: 399. The maximum permissible size of aggregate to be used in casing the ribs of a slab, is
explain: In ribbed slabs with thin sections, 10 mm aggregate is used to ensure the concrete can flow around the closely spaced reinforcement.

q: 400. If the diameter of longitudinal bars of a square column is 16 mm, the diameter of lateral ties should not be less than
explain: Lateral ties must be at least 1/4th the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar (16/4 = 4mm) but not less than 5mm (or 6mm in modern codes).

q: 401. A pre-cast pile generally used, is
explain: Square piles with chamfered corners are preferred because they are easy to cast and the chamfering prevents damage to the corners during driving.

q: 402. On piles, the drop must be at least
explain: The standard height of drop for a hammer in pile driving is generally maintained around 120 cm to provide sufficient energy without damaging the pile head.

q: 403. A very comfortable type of stairs is
explain: Open newel stairs provide a central well for ventilation and light, making them more spacious and comfortable for users.

q: 404. The minimum head room over a stair must be
explain: Note: In the options provided '200 mm' is marked as 'd' in the key, though technically 200 cm (2m) is the standard clearance for safety.

q: 405. For stairs spanning horizontally, the minimum waist provided is
explain: The waist slab thickness for horizontally spanning stairs is typically kept at a minimum of 8 cm to ensure structural rigidity.

q: 406. For stairs spanning l meters longitudinally between supports at the bottom and of a flight carrying a load w per unit horizontal area, the maximum bending moment per metre width, is
explain: Like a simply supported beam, a longitudinally spanning stair flight experiences a maximum moment of wl²/8.

q: 407. If longitudinally spanning stairs are casted along with their landings, the maximum bending moment per metre width, is taken as
explain: Casting with landings creates partial continuity, which reduces the effective maximum bending moment to approximately wl²/10.

q: 408. The number of treads in a flight is equal to
explain: In a flight of stairs, there is always one less tread than there are risers because the top tread is often part of the landing.

q: 409. An under-reinforced section means
options: steel is provided at the underside only
steel provided on one face only
explain: In an under-reinforced section, the steel reaches its yield stress before the concrete reaches its maximum compressive strain, providing ductile failure.

q: 410. An R.C.C. beam not provided with shear reinforcement may develop cracks in its bottom inclined roughly to the horizontal at
explain: Shear stress (diagonal tension) typically acts at a 45-degree angle to the beam axis, which is where cracks initiate if shear reinforcement is absent.

q: 411. In the zone of R.C.C. beam where stress in less than 5 kg/cm², nominal reinforcement is provided at a pitch of
options: one-half lever arm of the section
one-third lever arm of the section
one and half lever arm of the section
explain: Nominal stirrups are typically spaced at a distance equal to the lever arm (or slightly less) to bridge potential 45-degree cracks.

q: 412. The load stress of a section can be reduced by
options: increasing the total perimeter of bars
replacing larger bars by greater number of small bars
replacing smaller bars by greater number of greater bars
explain: Increasing the total perimeter of the reinforcement (by using more bars) improves the bond and reduces the bond stress between concrete and steel.

q: 413. An R.C.C roof slab is designed as a two way slab if
options: it supports loads in both directions
the ratio of spans in two directions is less than 2
the slab is continuous over two supports
the slab is discontinuous at edges
explain: If the aspect ratio (long span / short span) is less than 2, the slab significantly bends in both directions and must be designed as a two-way slab.

q: 414. The minimum number of main steel bars provided is R.C.C.
explain: Building codes specify minimum bars for geometry: 4 for rectangular, 6 for circular (to maintain the shape), and usually one per corner for polygons.

q: 415. Design of R.C.C. simply supported beams carrying U.D.L. is based on the resultant B.M. at
explain: For a simply supported beam with UDL, the maximum bending moment (wl²/8) occurs at the mid-span, which governs the flexural design.

q: 416. Design of R.C.C. cantilever beams, is based on the resultant force at
explain: In a cantilever beam, both the maximum bending moment and maximum shear force occur at the fixed support (the 'fixed end').

q: 417. Steel beam theory is used for
options: doubly reinforced beams ignoring compressive stress in concrete
beams if shear exceeds 4 times allowable shear stress
explain: Steel beam theory assumes that all compressive and tensile forces are carried by the steel reinforcement, ignoring the contribution of concrete in the compression zone.
